question.worked_solution:
At $x=5,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}(bx+4) \\  & =b(5)+4 \\  & =5b+4,\end{aligned}
$$

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {5}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {5}^{+}}(2x-1) \\  & =2(5)-1 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=5,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {5}^{+}}f(x) \\ 5b+4 & =9 \\ 5b & =5 \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=5$ for $b=1.$
